info.title: blygd API
info.description:
The write and reading API of blygd, a Blygger studio (protocol 0.4). It is studio-private, not protocol (§16.6): the public surface is each origin's static files. Spec references (§) are to blygger-spec docs/protocol-v0.4.md.

Every HTML string that came from another origin is returned verbatim; clients MUST sanitize it before rendering (§14). Responses that carry imported bytes include a notice saying so.

Authenticate with a bearer token. Each operation's security requirement names the one scope it needs; the owner token `*` holds every scope.

Finding the blyg: this host has no directory of blygs, and nothing is served at its root. Each blyg is mounted at its own path, `https://host/{handle}/`. `GET /api/me` returns the caller's `origin`, that base URL, and every public file (`blyg.json`, `feed.xml`, `items/index.json`, `items/{id}.json`) is relative to it.

Requests are budgeted per token and per user (a user's budget is twice a token's, across all their tokens). Each operation's `x-blygd-cost` names its class: `default` (120 a minute, bursts of 60), `fetch` (12 a minute; the call fetches from other hosts), `export` (2 a minute), `upload` (30 a minute, bursts of 20) and `stream` (no per-request budget; at most 8 open streams). Over budget is a 429 with `Retry-After`. An address that fails authentication too often is refused for a while, whatever token it then sends.

tags.name: filters
tags.description: A reader's private topics, judged by the classifier the operator configured, and what the reading feed does with posts about them. Never on the wire: the protocol has no AI in it, and a reader needs no models or keys (invariant 3).

get.summary: The calling token's user, scopes and origin.
A Server-Sent Events stream of change hints for this user.
get.description:
Each event names what changed, never the state: re-fetch what you show. Events, by type:

- `import` (needs reader:read): a poll of one of your subscriptions finished. `{subscription_id, items, more, error?}`, where `more` means a backfill continues with the next batch in about a minute.
- `subscribe` (needs reader:read): an entry of one of your subscription imports was tried. `{id, status, subscription_id?, error?}`, where status is subscribed, failed, or pending when it will be tried again.
- `item` (needs items:read): one of your items changed, from any client. `{id, change, version?, draft_rev?}`, where change is created, edited, deleted, published, withdrawn or pinned; version is the one published, withdrawn or pinned; and draft_rev is the draft's revision after a create, edit or publish, so a client can tell its own change from another's.
- `label` (needs reader:read): the classifier answered for an item of one of your subscriptions, so what your filters do to it may have changed. `{subscription_id, item_id}`.
- `mention` (needs mentions:read): an inbound mention to your origin arrived or changed. `{id, status, relation?}`.
- `outbound` (needs mentions:read): one of your outbound mentions was attempted. `{id, status, last_result}`.

A heartbeat comment arrives every 25 s. Events missed while disconnected are not replayed; fetch state on reconnect. Browsers should read this with fetch(), which can send the Authorization header; EventSource cannot. At most 8 streams per user.

200.description: The stream, until the client disconnects.

429.description: Too many open streams for this user.

patch.summary: Change origin settings and re-render the surface.

get.summary: The origin as a static deployment: a gzipped tar.
get.description: Every surface file at its origin-relative path, with directory pages (the feed page, permalink pages, pinned version pages) as `index.html`, plus every media file a published version references. Serve it at the origin's base URL: every URL inside is absolute against it. A static deployment advertises no Webmention endpoint (§15.1, §15.7), so the export is rendered with mentions off: no manifest `webmention` key and no `rel="webmention"` links, whatever the origin's setting. Pins are their stored bytes. Nothing is written. Drafts, hopper pages and the webmention endpoint are not part of it.

get.summary: List own items, newest activity first.

post.summary: Create a draft: a fragment, a thread, a stub (stub_of), or a fork (forked_from).
post.description: A fork without content_md fetches the pinned source (or reads it, if it is your own) and flattens it into the draft (§5.6 rule 6).

get.summary: An item with every published version.

patch.summary: Edit the draft, the next note, or generation metadata.
patch.description: Nothing changes on the wire until the next publish. With draft_rev, the edit applies only to the draft at that revision (409 stale otherwise), so two clients cannot overwrite each other unseen.

post.summary: Compose the draft as publishing it now would, and store nothing.
post.description: Composes the draft, or content_md in its place (an edit not yet saved), exactly as POST /api/items/{id}/publish would now: [TK] scopes stripped, [[id]] links resolved, and a thread's quotes baked from the versions they would quote, yours first, then your subscriptions' imports (§10.2). Nothing is stored, rendered to your surface, or sent. Every reason a publish would be refused is listed in problems, not returned as an error, and a directive that cannot bake is marked where it stands. It does not check a fork's pin at its origin, which only publishing fetches. Imports change as polls land, so a publish later may bake newer versions than this showed.

post.summary: Publish the draft as the next version.
post.description: Directives and [[id]] links resolve now: own items first, then your subscriptions' imports (§10.2). Every unresolvable one is listed in a 422's problems. 409 when nothing changed. 409 stale when draft_rev is sent and the draft has moved on, or when the draft changes while publishing.

patch.summary: Rename a hopper, or make it public or private.

post.summary: Add a reference to an own or imported item.
Upload an image: the raw bytes as the body, typed by Content-Type.

201.description: Stored, or already stored: the same bytes are the same object.

post.description: The declared type must match the bytes. Reference it from markdown as media/… ; publish checks every reference exists, and lists them in the item's media array.

delete.summary: Delete media no published version references.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Filter by class (§15.5): responses, or notices to hold apart.

parameters.name: include_blocked
parameters.description: Also list mentions from blocked sources.

put.summary: Show a verified mention on its target's page (§15.5).
put.description: Publishing a response is curation, never automatic, so this also needs origin:write. What shows: a verb, the source's author name, its host and a link; no words from the source. A notice is refused with 409: it is never shown among responses (§15.5).

delete.summary: Take a mention off its target's page.

post.summary: Block a host or a whole registrable domain.
post.description: Claims from a blocked source are answered like any other and dropped: nothing stored, nothing fetched. Mentions already received from it lose their approval at once.

delete.summary: Remove a block. Withdrawn approvals stay withdrawn.

get.summary: Outbound Webmentions, most recently changed first (at most 200).

post.summary: Subscribe by any URL; resolution follows §12.1.

422.description: Resolution failed; trail lists the URLs tried.

patch.summary: Rename for yourself, or publish/withdraw a blogroll entry.

delete.summary: Unsubscribe; drops any blogroll entry for it.

post.summary: Re-run resolution and report; changes nothing (§12.2).
Move to a confirmed new identity (§12.2).

422.description: Resolution failed, or to resolves elsewhere.

post.description: Within §12.3's etiquette: refused while the origin is backing off after failures, within a minute of its last poll (the mirror is shared by every subscriber), or while another poll of it runs. A refusal is 429 with Retry-After and retry_at.

200.description: Polled; the subscription as it now stands.

post.summary: Queue an OPML list of subscriptions.
post.description: Send an OPML document (a blogroll, §11, or another reader's export) as opml, or a url: an OPML file, or a blyg whose manifest names a blogroll (§6.1). Every entry with an http(s) xmlUrl, or an htmlUrl when it has none, is queued and resolved in the background like POST /api/subscriptions (§12.1), at most one per user at a time, so a long list costs no subscribe budget. A blyg's feed upgrades to the blyg itself (§11). Entries already queued or subscribed are left alone; failed ones are tried again. An entry's title becomes the subscription's display title when it differs from the origin's own and you have not named it. Imported subscriptions never join your blogroll (§11: inclusion is opt-in). Watch GET /api/subscriptions/imports, or the subscribe event.

delete.description: Forgets the entries in status, or all of them. No subscription changes, and a pending entry forgotten is never tried.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Cursor from a previous page's next.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: apply (the default) leaves out what your filters hide or hold, and counts it. off shows everything, each item still saying what your filters make of it.

get.summary: One imported item, with retained pins.

put.summary: Mark read at the current version.

post.summary: Mark read everything a feed could have shown.
post.description: Marks read, at its current version, every live item whose current version blygd first saw at or before as_of: everything a feed read at as_of could have shown, on every page. Send the as_of of the feed you showed. A version that arrives later stays unread, even one the origin dates earlier, which the feed sorts among items already read (§13.7). With subscription_id, only that subscription's items.

post.summary: Mint a token with a subset of your scopes.
post.description: Mints a token holding a subset of the caller's scopes, expiring no later than the caller does: a minted token never outlives its minter. A device token that expires is replaced by minting from a token that outlives it, usually the owner's, which never expires and belongs offline. There is no refresh: a long-lived tokens:write token kept on the device would be that credential.

delete.summary: Revoke the token making this request: sign out.
delete.description: Any token may end itself. Revoking another token takes tokens:write.

204.description: Revoked; the token no longer authenticates.

get.summary: Your filters, and whether the classifier runs.

post.description: Items the filter covers are classified in the background, newest first, back 14 days by feed position. Readers who wrote the same topic in the same words share one answer per item. At most 32 filters.

delete.summary: Delete a filter, and your overrides under it.

put.summary: Judge an item yourself under one of your filters.
put.description: Your judgment wins over the classifier's, for every version of the item.

delete.summary: Forget your judgment; the classifier's applies again.

bearer.description: A token minted by `blygd user add`, `blygd token mint` or POST /api/tokens. Scopes are listed per operation.

error.description: Stable code. invalid: a malformed request (400) or one refused as it stands (422). not_found: 404. conflict: 409. stale: the draft changed since the draft_rev sent (409); read it again. forbidden: the token lacks the operation's scope (403). unauthorized: no token, or one unknown, revoked or expired (401). unresolved: a URL that did not resolve (422, with trail). rate_limited: over a request budget, or too many failed authentications from this address (429). too_soon: a poll refused by §12.3's etiquette (429, with retry_at). too_many_streams: at most 8 open event streams per user (429). too_large: media over the upload cap (413). unavailable: events are not running (503). internal: the server's fault (500).

problems.description: Every reason a draft cannot be published (§10.2), on a 422 from publish.

trail.description: URLs tried, on a failed resolution (§12.1 step 6).

retry_at.description: When a refused poll may run (429 from poll).

at.description: The directive, link or [TK] scope at fault, as written.

origin.description: The caller's blyg base URL, `https://host/{handle}/`, with a trailing slash. Public files such as `blyg.json` are relative to it.

expires_at.description: When this token stops authenticating; null never.

author.description: Manifest author (§6.1), an object or null.

byline.description: Default per-item author (§5.5), an opaque object or null.

Selector.description: W3C text-quote selector of a partial transclusion (§10.3).

Cited.description: The human half of a citation (§5.9): frozen, self-asserted, never verified.

origin.description: Identity origin. Omitted in transclusions[] for own-origin sources (§10.3).

id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

StubOf.description: stub_of (§10.6): a blyg reference, or a plain-web {url}.

id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

StubTarget.description: What a new stub responds to. By id, the studio resolves the target (own items first, then your subscriptions; give origin to choose) and freezes version and cited. By url, cited is yours; retrieved defaults to now and the excerpt is held to 200 characters.

id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

origin.description: Identity origin of another origin's item; omitted for an own item (§5.7 rule 1).

id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

GenSource.description: A generation source (§5.7 rule 1): a reference to an item version the generator drew on. It resolves like a directive, so it may be another origin's item (rule 8).

GenMeta.description: What the client declares about one [TK] scope, by position.

content_html.description: For a thread, contains other origins' baked HTML verbatim (§10.2). Sanitize before rendering (§14).

links.description: One entry per resolved [[id]] link, in document order (§10.3a). Absent when the version has none, and on a withdrawal endcap.

id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

version.description: Latest published version; 0 for a draft.

page.description: Origin-relative permalink (§5.8), fixed at first publish.

draft_rev.description: Names the draft's state: draft_md, draft_note and generation. Send it back as draft_rev on PATCH or publish to change only the draft you saw. It is a hash, so equal drafts have equal revisions.

content_html.description: The current version's content_html, on GET /api/items only. Absent for a draft never published and for a withdrawn item. It bakes other origins' bytes (§10.2): sanitize before rendering (§14).

unpublished_changes.description: On GET /api/items only: present and true when a published item's draft differs from its current version, so publishing would change it.

kind.description: Default fragment; thread with stub_of; the source's kind for a fork without content.

forked_from.description: §5.6 lineage, immutable. Without content_md, the draft starts as the pinned source flattened (§5.6 rule 6).

stub_of.description: Makes the draft a stub (§10.6). Without content_md, a blyg stub starts as ![[id]].

note.description: Note for the next publish; empty clears.

generation.description: Per [TK] scope, by position; null clears.

draft_rev.description: Apply the edit only if the draft is still at this revision; otherwise 409 stale and nothing changes. Absent, the edit applies to whatever the draft holds.

note_generated.description: The client wrote the note, not the author (§5.2).

draft_rev.description: Publish only if the draft is still at this revision; otherwise 409 stale and nothing is published.

item_id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

MemberCreate.description: Exactly one of own_item_id or imported. An import is named by subscription_id, or by origin.

own_item_id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

target_item_id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

class.description: Set with relation (§15.5). A notice is a link, or a stub or transclusion from a document with no words of its own (a repost); it is never shown among responses and cannot be approved.

approved_at.description: Shown on the target's page since then (§15.5). Cleared when a re-verification finds the relation, class, origin, page or author changed, or the mention stops verifying.

blocked.description: The source is blocked. Such mentions are listed only with include_blocked=true.

source_item_id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

expires_at.description: When the token stops authenticating; null never.

scopes.description: Only scopes the calling token holds.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires. Absent, it expires with the minting token, or never if that never does. Never later than the minting token: a minted token cannot outlive its minter, as it cannot hold a scope its minter lacks.

expires_at.description: When it stops authenticating; null never.

id.description: The remote origin id; scopes imported item ids (§13.1).

origin.description: Identity origin (§12.2), or the final feed URL for L0.

author.description: The manifest's publication identity (§6.1), as the origin asserts it: an opaque object, name RECOMMENDED (§5.5). Relative URLs in it resolve against origin. Readers fall back to it when an item has no author. Null when the manifest has none, or for L0.

in_blogroll.description: Publishes or withdraws a blogroll entry (§11). Needs origin:write as well.

labels.description: One entry per enabled filter of yours that covers this item; empty when none does or no classifier is configured.

filtered.description: Null when the item shows plainly.

classification.description: none: no filter covers it (or no classifier is configured, or it is withdrawn). pending: some answer has not arrived. done. failed: the classifier cannot judge this version; it shows as if unfiltered.

next.description: Cursor for the next page; empty at the end.

as_of.description: When this page was read. Send the first page's to POST /api/reader/read to mark read what you showed and nothing that arrived since.

hidden.description: Items this page's stretch of the feed left out because a filter hides them. Each is counted on exactly one page. Zero with filters=off.

held.description: Items left out while a filter that holds waits for an answer.

Media.description: An uploaded object (§5.4). Its path is derived from its bytes, so it never changes meaning.

path.description: Origin-relative; write it in markdown as ![alt](media/…).

published.description: Referenced by a published version: served publicly and kept forever (§8 rules 2 and 4). Until then it 404s and may be deleted.

HopperPatch.description: At least one of name or public.

name.description: The slug follows the name until the hopper has ever been public.

public.description: Show the list at {origin}h/{slug}/ (§13.5): excerpts with attribution and links, served live, never part of the protocol surface. Going public freezes the slug for good. Needs origin:write as well.

kind.description: domain blocks the registrable domain and every subdomain of it.

value.description: A host, a domain, or a URL to take one from.

origin.description: The target's identity origin; omitted for an own item (§10.3a).

id.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

Link.description: A links[] entry (§10.3a): the item a resolved [[id]] link names. Not a reference: no version, no cited.

ItemDocument.description: The origin's items/{id}.json (§5), verbatim (jsonb orders its keys). blygd checked only that id names the item, kind is one it knows, and version is at least 1: every other member is the origin's unverified assertion, and members this description does not list may appear. Sanitize content_html (§14).

content_hash.description: Checked against content_md; a mismatch is the item's discrepancy (§13.3).

L0Document.description: A wrapped legacy RSS entry (§13.6). blygd's own shape, not a protocol document: it never leaves this instance except through this API. Mark it visibly as legacy content.

link.description: The entry's URL. A response to it is a {url} stub (§10.6).

summary_html.description: The entry's summary or description, verbatim and capped at 64 KB. Sanitize (§14).

summary_text.description: Plain text, cut to 1,000 characters (§5.3's fragment ethos).

ImportedDoc.description: The imported item's content: the origin's document for a blyg, blygd's wrapper for L0, or null once withdrawn (§13.4).

PinDocument.description: The origin's items/{id}/v{n}.json (§8), verbatim. blygd checked only that id and version name this pin and kind is not withdrawn; every other member is the origin's assertion. Sanitize content_html (§14).

as_of.description: The as_of of the feed you showed.

subscription_id.description: Only this subscription's items; absent, every subscription's.

marked.description: Items that were unread and are now read.

ImportRequest.description: Exactly one of opml or url.

opml.description: An OPML document, up to the 1 MB request limit.

url.description: An OPML file, or a blyg whose manifest names a blogroll.

entries.description: Entries with an http(s) URL, at most 1000.

queued.description: New entries, and failed ones queued again.

url.description: The entry's xmlUrl, or its htmlUrl.

title.description: The entry's text, as the list wrote it.

error.description: The last failure. A pending entry with one is waiting to try again; three failures and it fails.

content_md.description: Preview this in place of the saved draft; absent, the saved draft.
The wire content_md: [TK] scopes stripped to their output (§5.7). Empty when a scope has no output yet.

content_html.description: As publish would bake it, other origins' bytes included (§10.2). A directive that cannot bake is a blockquote of class "blyg-transclusion unresolved" saying why. Sanitize before rendering (§14).

problems.description: Every reason a publish would be refused now; empty means it would go through. A refusal of the draft as a whole is at "draft".

warnings.description: What a publish would warn about, such as a quote of an unpinned remote version.

name.description: The topic, in your words: "US politics", "spoilers for Severance season 3". A bare "spoilers" is refused: spoilers for what?

description.description: What you mean by it: what counts, what does not. Sent to the classifier with the name.

match.description: mentions: a post that mentions the topic at all matches. mainly: only a post mainly about it. Default mainly.

threshold.description: A post matches when the probability match names is at least this. Default 0.5. Changing it, match or action applies at once to the answers held; changing name or description asks the classifier again.

action.description: fold: shown, with filtered saying why, for the client to collapse. hide: left out of the feed and counted in hidden. Default fold.

pending.description: Before an answer arrives: show the post, or hold it back (counted in held) until it is answered, for at most 10 minutes after blygd first sees that version. A version the classifier cannot judge is never held. Default show.

subscription_id.description: Only this subscription's items; null, every subscription's.

enabled.description: A disabled filter is kept, and does nothing. Default true.

pending.description: Before an answer arrives: show the post, or hold it back (counted in held) until it is answered, for at most 10 minutes after blygd first sees that version. A version the classifier cannot judge is never held. Default show.

FilterPatch.description: Members to change; absent ones stay as they are.

subscription_id.description: Only this subscription's items; null, every subscription's.

enabled.description: A disabled filter is kept, and does nothing. Default true.

ClassifierStatus.description: Whether filters run on this instance. The operator configures the classifier (BLYGD_SUBQ_KEY); without one, filters are kept and do nothing.

model.description: The model answers come from; answers from another model are not used.

halted_until.description: No requests until then: the classifier refused the key, the credits ran out, or the model is not allowed. Items wait, unfiltered once any hold lapses.

calls_today.description: Requests so far this UTC day, across every reader.

matched.description: Your judgment: the item is, or is not, about the filter's topic.

Label.description: One of your filters that covers the item, and what is known.

matched.description: Whether the filter matches: your override when there is one, else the classifier's answer against the filter's match and threshold. Null: no answer yet for this version's words.

p_mentions.description: Probability the post at least mentions the topic.

p_mainly.description: Probability the post is mainly about the topic.

confidence.description: The classifier's confidence in its answer.

override.description: Your judgment, if you gave one (PUT /api/reader/items/{sid}/{iid}/filters/{fid}).

Filtered.description: What your filters do to the item.

action.description: hide wins over hold, and hold over fold.

Forbidden.description: The token lacks the scope this operation needs.

Conflict.description: Conflicts with current state, or an invariant refused the change.

Invalid.description: Well-formed but not acceptable; see message and, for publish, problems.

TooManyRequests.description: Over a request budget. Wait for Retry-After seconds. Budgets are per token and per user, by the operation's x-blygd-cost class; an address with too many failed authentications is refused too.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a request of this class is allowed.

schema.description: Item id (§5.1): 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32.

ImportedItemID.name: iid
ImportedItemID.description: Item id as scoped by the subscription; an L0 id is l0: plus hex.
